photos.c: Four of our leading walkers, Ray Hall, Ted Smith, Bob Barnes and Ray Middleton seen here together at the start of the 1960 Club 2 mile Championship. Both trophies, the "A.J Sawyer Memorial Cup" and the "Don Brown" style award were won by Ray Middleton, who is currently showing great form.

COVER PHOTO - (E.D.Lacey) Ray Middleton (here winning the Surrey 10) who, despite being troubled by an injured knee, has been our first man home in the L.C.C. '10', the Vidarians 15' and who also finished 3rd in the A.A.A 7 mile Track Championship.
RAY MIDDLETON admires the "Tommy Green" cup after receiving the award from the President.(Photo:Ed Lacey)
BACKPIECE (Photo:Ed Lacey) The start of the Olympic 50 Kilos at Tokyo showing, ringed, (L.to R.) Ray Middleton, Don Thompson and Paul Nihill, the silver medallist.
Don Thompson and Ray Middleton, both selected for Britain's Lugano Cup team, fight it out during the Met. W.C. Open 20 Kilos.
British Empire and Commonwealth Games silver-medallist Ray Middleton and the opening ceremony of the Games in Kingston, Jamaica.

Belgrave's Ray Middleton (2) and winner Ron Wallwork watch New Zealand's Norman Read receive his bronze medal during the 20 miles walk victory ceremony at the British Empire and Commonwealth Games, Kingston, Jamaica.
Ray Middleton leads Brian Keegan (London Vids) during his Championship win in the Surrey County 2 miles.
Gerry Cameron and Ray Middleton during the Club '20'

FRONTISPIECE: Members of Belgrave's victorious National R.W.A. '20' team display the Championship shield and the Nigmegan shield. L.toR: R. Coates,D.DeBondi,W.Wesch,P.Duncan,R.Middleton,L.Duquemin,J.Moullin. The absentee is R. Farley. Our walkers now hold three of the four National Championships.

Bert East (centre) had difficulty in even making the start of the London Transport '2' on July 6th at Acton, but mention the word "handicap" and he's off like a shot! Ray Middleton thinks it's a laugh beating the 2 miles record of a No.11 bus, while Wil Wesch gets on with winning at well over speed-limit
Wil Wesch, Carl Lawton and Ray Middleton finish 1st, 10th and 12th.
RIGHT: RAY MIDDLETON models his new "high collared sleeveless" look!
Front page: 1974 was a good year for Ray Middleton - winner of the London to Brighton, Hastings to Brighton and Accolade 8 Hour walks, setting five new world best performances in the latter.

Left: Two old warhorses and '64 Olympians cast an eye over today's walkers. Ken Matthews, 20k gold medallist, and our own Ray Middleton who was 13th in the 50k in 4:25:49.2, a time which was just outside the previous Olympic record.

photo.caption: Four of our leading walkers, Ray Hall, Ted Smith, Bob Barnes and Ray Middleton seen here together at the start of the 1960 Club 2 mile Championship. Both trophies, the "A.J Sawyer Memorial Cup" and the "Don Brown" style award were won by Ray Middleton, who is currently showing great form.
